title: Validate identifier consistency on modification save
gherkin:
Feature: Identifier consistency in reporting
  Scenario: Validate identifier consistency when saving modifications
    Given the system has an existing identifier
    When a user modifies the identifier
    Then the system must validate the identifier before saving the changes
    And the identifier must remain consistent across all reports
rationale: This test ensures that any modifications to identifiers are validated, maintaining consistency in reporting.
usedContextItems: The system must validate all changes before saving modifications to maintain identifier consistency.

From: internal_audit@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-03-08 14:00
Subject: Review findings on reporting consistency

Hi Dev Team,

During our recent reporting review, we found several consistency issues that need clarification before the reporting package can be considered reliable for audit use.

First, the financial outputs do not appear to align cleanly across all billing contexts. In some cases, the figures shown in reports, exported files, and billing records seem to reflect different presentation or calculation assumptions.

Second, the activity and audit views currently favor a privacy-preserving identifier style that makes operational review harder for non-technical auditors. We need to confirm whether this is the intended audit model, or whether authorized reviewers should have access to a controlled identity-resolution path.

Third, exported reporting artifacts do not always appear to match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform, which raises a broader question about which data representation should be treated as authoritative for audit purposes.

Please review and confirm the intended source-of-truth model for report generation, export, and audit visib

Date: 2026-02-22 11:00
Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)
